items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: they got this boy Earl Watkins to take my place.

ctx.x: Jimmy Archie? Lil' Jimmy Archie, yeah.

He was on trombone. I think he's still with Earl Hines, if I'm not mistaken. But he wasn't on that concert at Monterey, I think he was still at Muggsy Spaniel at the Hangover. Yeah. So you worked there for what, six weeks? See I worked with him for six weeks and they got this boy Earl Watkins to take my place. Because see my type of drumming and Earl's type of music didn't fit in together. See because I was, just like I said, I was more on the authentic side than what he was. Because he was kind of swinging his…
And this Earl Watkins was playing the more modern stuff.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: And so finally Doc found a drummer boy named Earl Watkins.

ctx.x: And so I went on out there and I worked with him for six weeks. And so finally Doc found a drummer boy named Earl Watkins.
